standard_prerequisites.name: The two-sided bound on the operator
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: The hypothesis of the statement, source line 2384
standard_prerequisites.use: It makes the square root of the operator a bounded operator from the space into the homogeneous order minus one space with bounded inverse, which is what allows the divergence in the source term to be absorbed.

standard_prerequisites.name: Duhamel's formula for the wave equation
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: The representation used in the proof at source lines 2401-2406
standard_prerequisites.use: It writes the solution as an integral of the sine propagator against the source terms, which is then estimated by spectral calculus.

core_obligations: Use the two-sided bound on the operator to see that its square root is a bounded operator into the homogeneous order minus one space with bounded inverse, and define the auxiliary field solving the square root of the operator applied to it equals the divergence of the second source term, with the same size as that term (proof lines 2398-2402).

Represent the solution by Duhamel's formula and rewrite the term involving the time derivative of the third source by integrating by parts, using that the third source vanishes at time zero, to obtain the display in which the sine propagator acts on the first and second sources and the cosine propagator on the third (proof lines 2402-2406).

Read off the first estimate from spectral calculus, and prove the energy estimate by differentiating the modified energy identity, substituting the equation and integrating by parts, then bounding the result by the size of the gradient of the solution times the size of the data; the two displays together are the statement (proof lines 2406-2413).
proof_roadmap: Absorbing the divergence into the auxiliary field (proof lines 2398-2402).
Duhamel representation and integration by parts (proof lines 2402-2406).
Spectral calculus for the first estimate and the energy identity for the second (proof lines 2406-2413).
